stories.headline: Alibaba opens Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B model with 6B active params that tops Opus 4.6 on coding

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on August 26, 2026, an open-weight multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model presented as the first public preview of the architecture that will power the Qwen4 family
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on August 26, 2026, an open-weight 125 billion parameter model that previews the architecture behind the coming Qwen4 family.

key_facts.fact: The model has 125B main parameters plus 51B N-gram embedding parameters, and activates only 6B parameters per token; Alibaba says it matches Qwen3.7-Plus at roughly one-ninth the training cost
key_facts.excerpt: 125B main model parameters, supplemented by an additional 51B N-gram embeddings, and 6B parameters activated per token... At ~ 1/9th the training cost, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves comparable capability against Qwen3.7-Plus, while being more capable in areas of coding and cowork.

key_facts.fact: On Alibaba's published benchmark table, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores 62.5 on SWE-bench Pro against Claude Opus 4.6 Max's 53.4, and 81.0 vs 77.5 on SWE-bench Multilingual
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores 62.5 on SWE-bench Pro against Claude Opus 4.6 Max's 53.4, and it also leads on SWE-bench Multilingual with 81.0 versus 77.5.

key_facts.fact: On agentic tests it posts 73.9 on CoWorkBench vs Opus 4.6 Max's 68.2 and 55.7 on JobBench vs 36.6, but trails Claude on Humanity's Last Exam (35.9 vs 40.0)
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next posts a 73.9 on CoWorkBench, ahead of Claude Opus 4.6 Max's 68.2, and a wide 55.7 on JobBench compared to 36.6 for the Anthropic model... The one place Claude pulls ahead in the agent section is Humanity's Last Exam, where Claude Opus 4.6 Max's 40.0 score beats Qwen's 35.9.

key_facts.fact: The checkpoint ships with a 262,144-token native context extensible to 1,000,000 tokens under the Qwen Community License 1.0, using a hybrid Gated DeltaNet plus Qwen Sparse Attention design
key_facts.excerpt: 262,144 native context, with the model card describing extension up to 1,000,000 tokens... Qwen Community License 1.0 listed on the model card... The repository highlights a hybrid Gated DeltaNet and Qwen Sparse Attention design.

key_facts.fact: The ModelScope teaser page went up on August 25 with a countdown pointing to a 23:00 Beijing time release for the standard and FP8 versions
key_facts.excerpt: The teaser page appeared on ModelScope on August 25. The release timer points to August 26 (Beijing time).

stories.headline: Z.ai says it built Ox Alpha, the free stealth model that topped OpenRouter, and opens the weights

key_facts.fact: China's Z.AI, also known as Zhipu, confirmed on Wednesday August 26 that the stealth model Ox Alpha is a new iteration of its GLM series and said it would release the weights that night
key_facts.excerpt: The company on Wednesday confirmed speculation that the Ox Alpha model is a new iteration of its GLM series and said it will release the weights for it tonight in response to queries by Bloomberg News.

key_facts.fact: Ox Alpha appeared uncredited on OpenRouter over the weekend and surged to the top of the leaderboard, more than doubling DeepSeek's usage — the biggest launch in that marketplace's history
key_facts.excerpt: Still free to use, Ox Alpha surged to the top spot on AI marketplace OpenRouter's leaderboard, more than doubling DeepSeek's use... Ox Alpha emerged over the weekend as an uncredited release on OpenRouter — the biggest launch in that marketplace's history.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter's rankings show Ox Alpha at 23.2 trillion tokens processed, against 11.6 trillion for second-place DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731
key_facts.excerpt: 1. Ox Alpha by stealth 23.2T tokens new | 2. DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 by deepseek 11.6T tokens

key_facts.fact: The model is a reasoning system built for coding and agentic tasks that accepts text, image and video input; Stripe CEO Patrick Collison called the stealth release 'very impressive'
key_facts.excerpt: It's a reasoning model designed for coding and agentic tasks, and it can process text, image and video input, according to its description. Patrick Collison, the CEO of Stripe Inc, which is acquiring OpenRouter, called the stealth-mode release 'very impressive'.

key_facts.fact: Ox Alpha listed on OpenRouter on August 20 at zero cost with a 1,048,576-token context window and 131,072 max output, offered by an undisclosed provider claiming capacity for 100 trillion tokens per day
key_facts.excerpt: Ox Alpha is an anonymous AI model that appeared on the OpenRouter API marketplace on August 20, 2026, priced at zero, backed by more than a million tokens of context... its provider had servicing capacity for 100 trillion tokens per day.

key_facts.fact: Before the confirmation, independent tokenizer forensics on 25 prompts had matched Ox Alpha's token counts to GLM-5.3 exactly apart from a fixed 75-token offset; Z.ai's statement named the GLM series but no specific product name
key_facts.excerpt: tokenizer counts had already matched GLM-5.3 exactly across 25 prompts (constant +75-token offset)... Z.ai's statement to Bloomberg named the GLM series, not a specific 'GLM-5.3-Flash' product, and no official model card had appeared as of this update.

key_facts.fact: Z.ai listed in January and files its first detailed earnings report on Monday, covering the six months since the IPO
key_facts.excerpt: The company files its first detailed earnings report then, covering the six months since it listed in January, and a free model at the top of the charts is an expensive way to make a point.

stories.headline: Bill Gates says AI crossed the bio, cyber and job-loss thresholds, urges a global framework

key_facts.fact: In an essay published August 26 on GatesNotes, Bill Gates writes that the transition to the AI era 'will be one of the most turbulent times in human history' and that 'right now, we are not preparing adequately'
key_facts.excerpt: The transition to the AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history. Right now, we are not preparing adequately for that transition.

key_facts.fact: Gates told MIT Technology Review that AI has already crossed the danger thresholds: 'We've crossed the threshold in terms of bio-capabilities, cyber-capabilities, psychosocial capabilities, job-market-destruction capabilities, and even the lack of control'
key_facts.excerpt: "We've crossed the threshold in terms of [AI's] bio-capabilities, cyber-capabilities, psychosocial capabilities, job-market-destruction capabilities, and even the lack of control," he said in an interview with MIT Technology Review about his new memo.

key_facts.fact: He argues any model capable of designing novel molecules should be monitored and says he views bioterrorism risk as 'about 50 times more scary, more likely than a natural pandemic risk'
key_facts.excerpt: "Any model that can make novel molecules should be monitored," he says. "I view bioterrorism risk, versus a natural pandemic, as about 50 times more scary, more likely than a natural pandemic risk."

key_facts.fact: The nearly 6,000-word essay proposes taxing AI tokens and robots to fund the social safety net and reserving certain jobs, such as elder care, for people under a label he calls 'Human Reserved'
key_facts.excerpt: Gates is back with a nearly 6,000-word essay... leads him to issue rare, concrete policy proposals: tax AI tokens and robots to disincentivize companies from replacing human staff and bolster social funds, and reserve specific jobs for people, a domain he calls 'Human Reserved.'

key_facts.fact: Gates calls for national bodies that set AI priorities across agencies plus a new international organization combining elements of nuclear inspection regimes, aviation regulation and ozone-layer agreements, and says it will require US-China cooperation
key_facts.excerpt: There's an inspections regime for nuclear weapons, regulations for international aviation, and agreements that protect the ozone layer. A new global organization for AI will need elements of all three and more... Some cooperation between the U.S. and China will be required.

key_facts.fact: Gates told the New York Times that industry leaders are privately alarmed but publicly quiet: 'In private, people who understand how good this stuff is, and how much better it's getting, they're very worried,' while in public they say 'don't say that. It's bad for us — the next trillion dollars we're trying to raise'
key_facts.excerpt: "In private, people who understand how good this stuff is, and how much better it's getting, they're very worried," he told the NYT. In public, though, they tell each other, "Hey, man, don't say that. It's bad for us - the next trillion dollars we're trying to raise."

key_facts.fact: He rejects industry self-regulation outright: 'Self-regulation on the most dangerous tool ever invented? No, thanks!'
key_facts.excerpt: "Self-regulation on the most dangerous tool ever invented? No, thanks!"

stories.headline: Anthropic to tell IPO investors its market tops $30 trillion, beating SpaceX's record pitch

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is expected to tell IPO investors its potential revenue opportunity exceeds $30 trillion, topping the $28.5 trillion SpaceX presented before its own listing, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Wall Street Journal
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is preparing to tell IPO investors that its potential revenue opportunity exceeds $30 trillion, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter. The figure would top the $28.5 trillion estimate SpaceX presented to investors ahead of its own offering.

key_facts.fact: The estimate is built from the full scope of work that could be done by AI models — counting human labour rather than software spending
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic arrives at it by looking at the full scope of work AI models could complete, the same people told the Journal. That framing counts human labour rather than software spending. This is how the number gets so large.

key_facts.fact: For scale, the 191 tech companies in the S&P 1500 generated $2.4 trillion in combined revenue last year, per FactSet data cited by the Journal
key_facts.excerpt: FactSet data cited by the Journal shows that the 191 tech companies in the S&P 1500 collectively generated $2.4 trillion in revenue last year.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic more than doubled revenue in Q2 to $11.6 billion, from $4.73 billion in Q1
key_facts.excerpt: Recently, the Claude maker more than doubled its revenue to $11.6 billion in Q2, up from $4.73 billion in Q1.

key_facts.fact: The company could raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation near $2 trillion, above SpaceX's $86 billion raise and $1.77 trillion debut in June
key_facts.excerpt: The Claude maker could also aim to raise as much as $100 billion in its offering and is targeting a valuation of about $2 trillion. Both marks would surpass what SpaceX achieved — the rocket company pulled in $86 billion and debuted at a $1.77 trillion valuation when it went public in June.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is expected to publish its IPO prospectus within weeks, leaving room for a debut as early as September or early October; it filed a confidential draft Form S-1 with the SEC on June 1
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is expected to file its IPO financial disclosure documents in the coming weeks, potentially paving the way for the company to go public as early as September or October. Anthropic had confidentially submitted a draft Form S-1 registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on June 1.

key_facts.fact: NYU finance professor Aswath Damodaran had said SpaceX's AI-heavy market estimate was 'reaching the end of what's plausible and pushing beyond'
key_facts.excerpt: New York University finance professor Aswath Damodaran said ahead of SpaceX's offering that the AI TAM figure was 'reaching the end of what's plausible and pushing beyond.'

stories.headline: Meta's secret plan to cut teams 60% and run on AI agents collapsed as the agents underdelivered

key_facts.fact: At Zuckerberg's January leadership retreat in Hawaii, Meta hatched 'Project OT' (Organization Transformation), a plan for an 'AI native' company where AI would take over much of the daily work of thousands of employees, overseen by smaller 'talent-dense' human teams
key_facts.excerpt: Code-named Project OT – short for Organization Transformation – the plan envisioned an 'AI native' future for the owner of Facebook and Instagram. AI would take over much of the daily work performed by thousands of human employees. Virtual workers would be overseen inside Meta by smaller, 'talent-dense' cadres of human staffers.

key_facts.fact: Scenario-planning explored shrinking many teams by as much as 60%, in two waves — a first purge in May and a second in November
key_facts.excerpt: In scenario-planning exercises, two of these people said, executives explored slashing the size of many teams across Meta by as much as 60 per cent... The restructuring would be carried out in two 'waves,' beginning with a first purge in May and followed by another shakeup in November.

key_facts.fact: On the night of May 19, hours before the first layoff wave, Zuckerberg called off the November round; Meta still cut 10% of its workforce the next day
key_facts.excerpt: But on the night of May 19, just hours before the first layoff wave, Zuckerberg blinked. Meta laid off 10 per cent of its employees the next day, but it called off planning for the November cuts.

key_facts.fact: Internal posts showed AI-driven code changes to internal platforms up 220% year-over-year while changes that reached users rose only 36%
key_facts.excerpt: code changes made to the internal software platforms and infrastructure employees use on the job were up 220% year-over-year, according to a post by Bosworth in early June. But changes that led to new or upgraded features reaching Meta users were only up 36%.

key_facts.fact: An April internal post said unchecked AI agents were performing 'large-scale, disruptive actions that humans are unlikely to execute'; major technical and security incidents rose 40% year-over-year and firefighting time was up 70%
key_facts.excerpt: Another post, in April, said that unchecked AI agents were performing 'large-scale, disruptive actions that humans are unlikely to execute.' The result: Major technical and security incidents, such as service disruptions and possible data leaks, spiked 40 per cent from the previous year, with the time staffers had to spend 'firefighting' them up 70 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Meta confirmed Project OT existed and that the most drastic scenarios involved cutting some teams by up to 60%, but said it never intended to lay off 60% of its whole workforce
key_facts.excerpt: The company acknowledged that some scenarios considered reductions of up to 60% in certain teams, through both layoffs and redeployments, but said several major units were not involved.

key_facts.fact: Meta had mandated tracking software on US employees' devices to capture keystrokes and mouse clicks to teach its AI agents to mimic humans, fuelling the internal revolt
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters also reported in April that Meta had mandated that tracking software be installed on US employees' devices to capture their keystrokes and mouse clicks to teach its AI agents to replicate how humans interact with computers.

key_facts.fact: At a July town hall Zuckerberg conceded AI agent technology had not 'accelerated' as fast as he expected but predicted benefits within three to six months
key_facts.excerpt: In early July, Zuckerberg made a surprise appearance at an internal town hall and conceded miscalculations on the reorganisation's timing. AI agent technology, he said, had not 'accelerated' as quickly as he had anticipated.

stories.headline: DeepSeek's revenue hit $70.7M in seven months, 10x all of 2025, as it raises at a $74B valuation

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek generated about 475 million yuan ($70.7 million) in revenue in the first seven months of 2026, roughly ten times its full-year 2025 total, The Information reported citing people familiar with the matter
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek generated about 475 million yuan (HK$513 million) in revenue during the first seven months of this year, representing roughly a tenfold jump from 2025, tech publication The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The company posted a net loss of about 715 million yuan over the seven months, after a full-year 2025 net loss of 935 million yuan
key_facts.excerpt: The company recorded a net loss of around 715 million yuan in the seven-month period, following a full-year net loss of 935 million yuan in 2025, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek is in talks with existing and potential investors to raise 50 billion yuan in a second round valuing it at 500 billion yuan (about $74 billion)
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek is currently in talks with existing and potential investors to raise 50 billion yuan in a second funding round that would value the firm at 500 billion yuan, the report said.

key_facts.fact: Gross margin was 44.6% overall and 82.9% on API sales, but the lab spent about 11 billion yuan (~$1.6 billion) on infrastructure in the same seven months — nearly ten times the 1.2 billion yuan spent in all of 2025
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek spent about RMB 11 billion — roughly $1.6 billion — on infrastructure in the seven months through July, nearly ten times the RMB 1.2 billion it spent in all of 2025, on server leases and chip purchases. Seven months of revenue was RMB 475 million.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek closed a first external round in late May at a post-money valuation near $52 billion and has hired banks for a Shanghai listing targeted for 2027
key_facts.excerpt: It closed its first external round in late May at a post-money valuation near $52 billion, roughly $7 billion raised from a group Reuters described as a state-aligned industrial coalition — Tencent, battery maker CATL, China's national AI fund, NetEase and JD.com... It is now targeting close to $8 billion more at about $74 billion, and has hired banks toward a Shanghai listing targeted for 2027.

stories.headline: China's Moonshot seeks 30% of cloud revenue from Microsoft, Amazon and Google to host Kimi K3

key_facts.fact: Moonshot AI is negotiating revenue-sharing agreements with Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet's Google to let the US cloud giants host its Kimi K3 model, three people familiar with the talks told Reuters
key_facts.excerpt: China's Moonshot AI is negotiating revenue-sharing agreements with Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet's Google that would allow the U.S. cloud giants to host its blockbuster Kimi K3 model, three people familiar with the talks said.

key_facts.fact: The IPO-bound company is seeking up to a 30% share of revenue generated from K3-related services on Azure, AWS and Google Cloud
key_facts.excerpt: IPO-bound Moonshot is seeking up to a 30% share of revenue generated from K3-related services on Microsoft's Azure, Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, according to the sources.

key_facts.fact: Any deal would be the first big revenue-sharing pact between a Chinese AI firm and a major US cloud company; talks are early and unresolved issues include the revenue split, data access and auditing token usage
key_facts.excerpt: Any deal could mark the first big revenue-sharing pact between a Chinese AI firm and a major U.S. cloud company... unresolved issues in Moonshot's negotiations with the U.S. cloud companies include how revenue might be split, data access and auditing token usage.

key_facts.fact: The 30% cut inverts the usual arrangement in which the platform takes the cut and the model developer receives the remainder
key_facts.excerpt: A 30% share is aggressive, though it reportedly matches what Moonshot has been asking large customers. It also inverts the usual arrangement, in which the platform takes the cut, and the developer receives the remainder.

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said last month he might add Moonshot to a trade blacklist; US officials have accused the company of stealing from Anthropic's Fable model to build Kimi K3 and of illegally acquiring Nvidia chips
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot has come under fire from U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent who said last month that he might add it to a trade blacklist. U.S. officials have accused the Beijing-based company of stealing from Anthropic's most sophisticated model, Fable, to help create Kimi K3 and illegally acquiring Nvidia chips.

key_facts.fact: Moonshot has already signed similar revenue-sharing agreements with smaller cloud platforms, and Chinese IT services provider Chinasoft International disclosed one in July
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot has signed similar agreements with some smaller cloud platforms, the sources said, without providing details. In July, Chinese IT services provider Chinasoft International said it had a revenue-sharing agreement with Moonshot.

stories.headline: Huawei bids to export 1,408 Ascend 950 chips to Egypt as US assembles a counteroffer

key_facts.fact: Huawei responded to a tender from Cairo with a proposal to export 1,408 of its top-end Ascend 950-series chips for an AI training cloud, plus 600 more Ascend 950 or 910B chips for two inference clusters, under a 12-month buildout plan.
key_facts.excerpt: China's top competitor to Nvidia Corp. responded to a tender from Cairo with a proposal to export 1,408 of its top-end Ascend 950-series chips for an AI training cloud, plus 600 more of either those chips or the earlier 910B model to be used for two inference clusters... Huawei laid out a 12-month plan to build the infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: The data centers would serve military, surveillance and other public-sector uses, and the deal would be the first known export of Huawei's Ascend accelerators after more than a year of attempts.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei Technologies Co has pitched the Egyptian government on building AI data centres for military, surveillance and other public sector use... It also could be the first known export of Huawei's Ascend accelerators after more than a year of attempts.

key_facts.fact: US officials are assembling a consortium including Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft to counter the bid; it may be the first time the US and China compete directly for the same government AI data center tender.

key_facts.fact: The proposal is a partnership with iFlytek and includes vehicle and individual recognition tied to a national population database, presented in a 102-page deck; both firms have been on the US blacklist since 2019.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei's Egypt proposal involves a partnership with iFlytek Co, the Chinese surveillance giant that along with Huawei has been blacklisted by the US since 2019. Among the firms' offerings are vehicle and individual recognition based on a national population database... On one slide of the 102-page presentation, examples of 'basic video applications' contain the insignia of China's Ministry of Public Security.

key_facts.fact: AI chip shipments to Egypt have required Washington's permission since 2023, and roughly 2,000 Huawei 950DT accelerators equal only a few hundred top Nvidia chips in training capability.

stories.headline: HP licenses Huawei's Wi-Fi patents in a multi-year global cross-licensing deal

key_facts.fact: Huawei and HP announced on August 26, 2026 a multiyear global patent cross-licensing agreement that includes a license to HP for certain Huawei Wi-Fi patents.
key_facts.excerpt: [Shenzhen, China, August 26, 2026] Today, Huawei and HP Inc. announced the signing of a multiyear global patent cross-licensing agreement, including license to HP Inc. for certain Huawei WiFi patents.

key_facts.fact: The cross-license covers patents used in Wi-Fi technology including the latest Wi-Fi 7 standard, gives Huawei access to HP patents in return, and neither company disclosed financial terms.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Huawei Technologies said on Wednesday it had reached a multi-year cross-licence agreement with HP Inc, covering patents used in Wi-Fi technology, including the latest Wi-Fi 7 standard. The deal gives HP access to Huawei patents and gives Huawei access to HP patents, though neither company disclosed financial terms.

key_facts.fact: HP played down the deal, calling it a routine standard-essential patent license and 'not a broader strategic or commercial relationship, partnership, or collaboration with Huawei.'
key_facts.excerpt: "This is a standard-essential patent license covering Wi-Fi technology - something used broadly across the industry and routine for companies whose products connect to Wi-Fi. It is not new, does not represent a broader strategic or commercial relationship, partnership, or collaboration with Huawei," HP said.

key_facts.fact: The agreement follows Huawei's 2025 lawsuit against HP over Wi-Fi 6 patents; the dispute was resolved in November 2025 when HP joined Sisvel's Wi-Fi 6 pool of about 2,000 patents.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement came after Huawei filed a lawsuit against HP in 2025 over Wi-fi 6 patents, but the disputes were resolved in November last year after the American PC maker became a licensee of the patent pool of Italian intellectual property management firm Sisvel.

key_facts.fact: The deal is a sign of adoption of Huawei technology outside China despite the US placing the company on its blacklist in 2019.
key_facts.excerpt: It's a sign of adoption of Huawei's technology outside China, despite the U.S. blacklisting the company in 2019, a move that restricted it from working with American suppliers such as Google.

stories.headline: Skild AI unveils S1, a robot model that learns 10-minute unseen tasks from a single video

key_facts.fact: Skild AI announced S1 on August 25, 2026: a robotic foundation model that takes a single video demonstration as its prompt and executes the task with no fine-tuning and no post-training.
key_facts.excerpt: Skild AI announced S1 on 25 August 2026, a robot foundation model that learns a new task from a single human video... S1 takes one egocentric human video as its prompt and carries out the task with no fine-tuning and no post-training, so the weights never change.

key_facts.fact: In a controlled comparison holding data, architecture and compute constant, the video-prompted model scored 66% on unseen tasks versus 9% for a language-prompted policy trained on the same 100,000-hour dataset.
key_facts.excerpt: The company reports a 66% success rate on unseen tasks, compared with 9% for a language-prompted model trained on the same 100,000-hour dataset.

key_facts.fact: Skild says one video demonstration was worth roughly 380 post-training episodes; the language-prompted model needed an estimated 380 demonstrations to match the in-context result.
key_facts.excerpt: The in-context model reached a 66% success rate from one prompt. The language-prompted model needed an estimated 380 post-training demonstrations to reach the same result.

key_facts.fact: The four demonstrated tasks absent from pre-training — plant potting, pancake cooking, pour-over coffee and kit assembly — run up to ten minutes and span dozens of manipulation steps, with unseen tasks showing a 7x gain over language prompting.
key_facts.excerpt: S1 performs tasks that run up to ten minutes and do not appear in the training data. ICL scaling gains over language prompting are moderate for seen tasks, but unseen tasks experience a 7x performance improvement.

key_facts.fact: There are no downloadable weights, no public API and no paper; Skild is deploying S1 with industrial partners including ABB Robotics, Universal Robots and MiR.
key_facts.excerpt: There are no downloadable weights, no public API, no licence and no pricing. Skild says it is deploying S1 with a limited set of industrial partners now... Its named robot OEM partners are ABB Robotics, Universal Robots and MiR.

key_facts.fact: S1 was trained on Nvidia AI infrastructure, and Skild says the model must infer the demonstrator's intent because the demo may come from a different scene, viewpoint or robot body.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the demonstration may come from a different scene, viewpoint, or embodiment, the policy must implicitly learn the demonstrator's intent, functional correspondences, and task progress... S1 is built on NVIDIA AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches Jetson Orin Nano 2, doubling entry-level robot compute at 40% less power

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced Jetson Orin Nano 2 on August 25, 2026 at Hot Chips, a robotics computer for entry-level edge AI aimed at robots, delivery and inspection drones, and vision AI systems.
key_facts.excerpt: August 25, 2026 - NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 2, a new robotics computer for entry-level edge AI, enables millions of developers worldwide to build robots, delivery and inspection drones, and vision AI systems for frontier physical AI applications.

key_facts.fact: The module delivers 78 trillion operations per second of AI compute with 8GB of memory and an 8-core Arm CPU.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial, Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy delivered median overall survival of 26.4 months versus 19.2 months for trastuzumab plus chemotherapy — a 28% reduction in the risk of death and the longest median OS reported in a Phase 3 trial in this setting.

key_facts.fact: Meta will book a legal expense of roughly $10 billion in Q3 2026 for the deal — a charge it says was not contemplated in the expense range given on its Q2 earnings call.
key_facts.excerpt: We expect to accrue a legal expense of approximately $10 billion in Q3'26 related to the agreement. This charge was not contemplated in the expense range that was provided in the Q2 earnings call.

key_facts.fact: The Verge, reading the settlement terms, puts the payment at $17.1 billion over 10 years with the same $5.3 billion contingent on YouTube and TikTok, and says the trial Meta escaped could have cost it hundreds of billions.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta will also agree to pay $17.1 billion to states over a period of 10 years. The company outlined its obligations in a blog post, noting that $5.3 billion of this money will only be paid out if YouTube and TikTok implement their own daily time limits and each pay an equivalent amount to that figure.

key_facts.fact: The court filing itself says Meta agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion, and states in the filing that it 'denies the allegations against it and that it has any liability to the Plaintiffs.'
key_facts.excerpt: A court filing indicates that Meta agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion to bring the case to an end. The filing also says that the company "denies the allegations against it and that it has any liability to the Plaintiffs," which are a collection of 29 states.

key_facts.fact: California AG Rob Bonta's office describes a $17 billion figure over 10 years resolving the claims of 51 attorneys general, and requires Meta to accept an independent auditor plus an injunction barring further false or misleading statements about its safety features.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed settlement would require Meta to pay $17 billion in penalties to the states over 10 years... Meta must also bring on an independent auditor with "expansive access to information and resources"... and would also be subject to an injunction "prohibiting it from making further false, misleading, or deceptive statements around its safety features."

key_facts.fact: Product terms: a default two-hour daily time limit cumulative across Facebook and Instagram that teens can only lift with a parent's permission (counted even across multiple detected accounts), and a Night Mode default block from midnight to 6am covering Feed, Stories, Explore and Reels.
key_facts.excerpt: Time Limit: A default two-hour daily time limit that teens can only turn off with a parent's permission. This limit is cumulative across Facebook and Instagram... Night Mode: A default block from our apps between midnight and 6am. This means teens will not be able to post or view their Feed, Stories, Explore, or Reels, for example.

key_facts.fact: Also required: notifications muted by default 8am–3pm ('School Mode'), prompts every 15 minutes of continuous use and at 60 and 90 minutes of daily use, an opt-in non-algorithmic feed as default, hidden like counts, autoplay off, and a ban on cosmetic-surgery and extreme makeup filters for teens. Direct messages are exempt from the time, night and school restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: School Mode: Notifications will be muted by default between 8 AM and 3 PM... Regular Prompts: Teens will receive prompts after every 15 minutes of continuous screen time... Algorithmic Feed Control: Teens will be able to choose a non-algorithmic feed... Our direct messaging features are excluded from Night Mode, Time Limit, and School Mode restrictions.

key_facts.fact: Meta must build an age-assurance standard subject to independent testing with a false-positive rate no higher than 10% for 16–17-year-olds and 3% for 13–15-year-olds, and must incorporate age signals from Apple's and Google's operating systems and app stores.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta agreed to come up with an age assurance standard that is subject to independent testing, and must have a false positive rate no higher than 10 percent for users aged 16 to 17, and 3 percent for users aged 13 to 15.

key_facts.fact: Users who claim to be over 18 but do not complete the age assurance test within two weeks get account restrictions and age-appropriate content recommendations; Meta must also try to link accounts held by a single user to stop circumvention, and provide an appeals process.
key_facts.excerpt: Users who say they're over 18 but don't complete the age assurance test within two weeks will have restrictions on their accounts meant to "restrict potential adult bad actors" from contacting teens... The agreement requires Meta to try to link accounts owned by a single user to prevent circumvention of its new rules, and provide an appeals process for users.

key_facts.fact: The majority of the terms must stay in place for 10 years, and apply automatically to under-18s on Instagram and Facebook in participating states and territories, pending judicial approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Pending judicial approval, in participating US states and territories, these protections and controls will automatically apply to under-18s on Instagram and Facebook. The majority of the terms are required to remain in place for 10 years.

key_facts.fact: Meta is publicly pressuring rivals to match the terms: chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney called on TikTok and YouTube to implement the framework 'right away' because teens move fluidly across dozens of apps.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our new Time Limit commitments, Night Mode features and usage limits during school hours set the right path forward for our whole industry, but this framework will only work if all our peers join us," Meta's chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: The settlement landed mid-trial in the second week of a federal trial in Oakland brought by 29 states, co-led by California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey; Meta shares rose about 5% in premarket trading, and California alone could receive $1.5–2.1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of the settlement, Meta agreed to pay $16.7 billion. The state of California could receive $1.5 billion to $2.1 billion if the court officially approves the settlement... Shares of the social media giant gained 5% during premarket trading after the news broke.

key_facts.fact: The trial began 2026-08-18 in Oakland and was expected to run into early October, with Mark Zuckerberg expected to testify; Instagram head Adam Mosseri had testified the day before the settlement.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial started last week in federal court in Oakland, Calif., and was expected to run through early October. But the settlement announcement comes only midway through the trial's second week.

stories.headline: Pennsylvania sues Snap over Snapchat's addictive design and its 13+ app-store rating

key_facts.fact: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday sued Snap Inc. on 2026-08-25, accusing it of failing to protect children from compulsive use of Snapchat and of lying about how often adult-themed content appears on the app.
key_facts.excerpt: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R) announced a lawsuit Tuesday, accusing Snap, the parent company of Snapchat, of failing to protect children from compulsively using its platform. The complaint, filed this week, alleges Snapchat knowingly lies about the frequency of adult-themed material like drug use or sexual content to maintain a 13+ app rating in app stores.

key_facts.fact: The 49-page complaint was filed in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas under Pennsylvania's Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, seeking declaratory relief, a permanent injunction, civil penalties for willful violations and costs.
key_facts.excerpt: IN THE PHILADELPHIA COURT OF COMMON PLEAS... COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY AND INJUNCTIVE RELIEF... This is an action for statutory and equitable relief under the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law (UTPCPL), 73 P.S. Section 201-1, et seq.

key_facts.fact: The core allegation is that Snap answers Apple's App Store rating questionnaire in a way that yields a 13+ rating (and a 'Teen' rating on Google Play and the Microsoft Store) while sexual content, drug references and mature themes are readily available and even recommended to users known to be 13.
key_facts.excerpt: when Snap makes the Snapchat app available in Apple's App Store, it answers a rubric of questions provided by Apple, and in doing so, tells Pennsylvania consumers that Snapchat is rated "13+"... In fact, content on Snapchat in Apple's age-rating categories just described is easily available and even recommended by Snap to users known to be as young as 13 years old.

key_facts.fact: The complaint targets specific engagement mechanics — ephemeral content, infinite scroll, push notifications, autoplay, Snapscores and Snapstreaks — as deliberate drivers of behavioral addiction in minors.
key_facts.excerpt: Snapchat also publishes personal interactive metrics like "Snapscores" and "Snapstreaks," which grade a user's frequency of engaging with... All of these design choices lead to behavioral addiction among young Snapchat users, which harms their mental and physical health.

key_facts.fact: Sunday said the streak feature 'puts a tangible value on friendships and influences a child's feelings of self-worth,' and that the suit's goal is an overhaul of how Snapchat is marketed and advertised.
key_facts.excerpt: "We allege this streak feature puts a tangible value on friendships and influences a child's feelings of self-worth," he said... "This is a very serious legal action with the end goals of being an overhaul of how Snapchat markets and advertises its app."

key_facts.fact: This is Sunday's second social-media suit in a month — he sued TikTok on 2026-08-11 on similar consumer-protection grounds — and he said his office is 'actively looking at other companies as well.'
key_facts.excerpt: For the second time this month, Sunday filed a lawsuit against a social media company. After targeting TikTok on Aug. 11, Sunday announced Tuesday that he was filing suit against Snapchat... "I don't want to go into great detail on that, but I will tell you that we are actively looking at other companies as well."

key_facts.fact: The complaint says users open Snapchat an average of 30 times a day; Pew data cited at the press conference puts Snapchat use at 55% of American teens, roughly 450,000 of Pennsylvania's 807,000 teenagers.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a December 2025 report from the Pew Research Center, 55% of American teens use Snapchat – a statistic that means roughly 450,000 of the state's 807,000 teenagers are on the app – and, Sunday said, those users open the app an average of 30 times a day.

key_facts.fact: Snap rejected the suit, saying the allegations 'fundamentally misrepresent' the platform and noting Snapchat opens to a camera rather than a content feed.
key_facts.excerpt: "Snapchat was designed differently from the beginning: it opens to a camera, not a feed of content, and was built to encourage self-expression and authentic connection with friends," the spokesperson told The Hill.

key_facts.fact: Pennsylvania joins at least seven other states — Arkansas, Florida, Kansas, Nevada, New Mexico and Texas among them — that have already brought legal action against Snap over child-safety failures.
key_facts.excerpt: Pennsylvania is far from the first state to try to bring Snap to heel. Seven other states – Arkansas, Florida, Kansas, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas and Nevada – have brought legal action against the company.
